text:
Oh swift one, I love you.

Oh hurried fox at the edge of the dress
and sharp boundary of the insulting boot,
Artemis's knee fleeting among the stone,
I love you,
fugitive shadow on the noble staircase,
back amid trumpets on the bridge.

Oh vague ones, I envy you,
paired images in the gray
vapors of the half-closed panes,
impatient
—arriving late for appointments—
nerves of those who inhabit (the
safe, arrogant carelessness of the half-open door
and the ordering gesture of things that look).

I want almost everything:
the palace door with arms and figures,
the name of kings and the brass of the Republic.
I want your eyes, ingenuous foreigner,
and the soulless ease of the copyist.
I want this light of now. It is my desire
to be open, attentive, until I leave.
And I would like someone to tell me
goodbye,
contained, laughing through tears.


Stranger at the doors, you are not alone,
my hurried sadness accompanies you.

translation.title: The Square Court
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering of the French-titled poem. The title’s French form is rendered in English, while the rapid figures, palace imagery, and closing address are preserved.
